heroHeadline: China Restricts AI Talent Travel at DeepSeek and Alibaba — Two-Vector Lock-In as Big Fund Investment + Travel Bans Secure China's AI Researcher Pool
heroSubtitle: May 27, 2026 — China formally expanded overseas travel restrictions to cover senior AI researchers and engineers at private tech firms including DeepSeek and Alibaba (Bloomberg, May 26), requiring government approval before traveling abroad — an extension of controls previously limited to state employees and defense researchers. The expansion is a structural complement to DeepSeek's ~$50B Big Fund-led funding round (closed May 22): financial retention via state capital + mobility restriction via travel controls = Beijing's two-vector talent lock-in strategy. The week's other major developments: DeepSeek made permanent its 75% price cut on V4 Pro ($0.003625/M input tokens — less than 1/10th of OpenAI GPT-5.5, and Semafor noted below Western rivals' compute cost for equivalent capability), deepening the global AI price war as the funding round closes. Qualcomm struck an AI data center ASIC chip supply deal with ByteDance (Bloomberg, May 26) — ByteDance's first major external chip supplier for AI infrastructure; Qualcomm shares jumped 6.8% to an all-time high. SMIC's $6B ($5.97B) acquisition of Semiconductor Manufacturing North China (SMNC) received CSRC final approval (May 22–23), consolidating ~900K wafers/month of mature-node capacity under a single fully state-aligned entity — the largest STAR Market tech deal in history. These developments build on the week's semiconductor milestone: global analysts on May 27 assessed Huawei's Tau Scaling Law (unveiled May 25 at IEEE ISCAS 2026 in Shanghai) as potentially 'Another DeepSeek Moment' — SCMP, Bloomberg, and Tom's Hardware all published major analysis pieces describing LogicFolding's architectural bypass of ASML EUV lithography as a paradigm shift in China's long-horizon chip strategy, not merely a technical announcement. China's semiconductor and AI architecture is now multi-vector across every layer: model efficiency (DeepSeek V4 Pro at commodity pricing), chip hardware (Huawei Ascend 950PR ~$12B 2026 revenue, Alibaba Zhenwu M890 560K+ units), foundry consolidation (SMIC-SMNC unified, SMIC 7nm targeting 50K wafers/month by June), chip design engineering (Tau Scaling Law/LogicFolding for 2031 horizon), and talent lock-in (financial via Big Fund + legal via travel controls). The Qualcomm-ByteDance ASIC deal provides one data point against full decoupling: below the export control threshold, US chipmakers can still supply the world's highest-token-volume AI platform with specialized inference silicon — but ByteDance's primary AI chip commitment ($5.6B Huawei Ascend order) is now firmly domestic.
